definition: An outright position is a directional bet on a single commodity's price — for example, betting that electricity prices will rise or fall relative to current expectations of future prices.
core_idea: Taking an outright position means being exposed to the absolute price direction of one commodity, as opposed to the relative relationship between two commodities.
key_points: An outright trade is a single-commodity directional bet.
Contrasted directly with spread trades, which bet on the relationship between two related products instead of absolute direction.
trading_implications: Outright positions carry full exposure to commodity price volatility and therefore typically require more margin than an equivalent spread position.
